Title: Tacy Borg
Paragraphs: Portfolio

Title: Artist Statement
Paragraphs: An artist's craft is to take risks: to surrender to the unfolding of the material and approach a knowledge that arrives across multiple times—past, present and future. Each pixel-art mosaic is handmade, using a language of craft and technology to explore the emotions, intuitions and mental journeys of a human system governed by a digital world. I attach colored metal studs to a wooden base, folding them beforehand to make assembly easier. Each stud acts as a unit of color that combines with the others to form spirals, bodies, lines, circles and the other shapes that make up the finished piece.

Tacy Borg is the artist name created for this project. It joins two essential parts of its message: “Ta”, a syllable from Natalia (the human, imperfect, traumatized), and “cy borg”, meaning cybernetic organism (the sophisticated, divine, transhuman). Ultimately, this entire body of work is the expression of an organism adapting to an environment conceived at a higher level.

Title: Biography
Paragraphs: Tacy Borg (Medellín, 1988) is a contemporary artist who graduated in Visual Arts from Pontificia Universidad Javeriana in Bogotá, specializing in audiovisual practice. Her work investigates identity and memory, and their convergence through the materials she uses. Precious and industrial metals, wood and paper, alongside photography and video, are central to her current practice. She has exhibited nationally and internationally, including the Primavera 2026 exhibition of Colombian artists, the Watermill Center Foundation in New York in 2013, and the national student exhibition of the UNESCO Chair in Communication and Ventanas 2010.

Columns.Title: Conceptual research
Paragraphs: Memory and identity. An exploration of family memories, cultural inheritance, decolonization and the construction of the self through portraiture.

Columns.Title: Technical research
Paragraphs: The artist creates small-format pieces in precious metals and mosaics in hand-painted industrial metals. Her handmade jewelry practice includes piercing, soldering, weaving, chasing, casting and other techniques. She also develops her drawing in graphite and charcoal, watercolor painting, experimental analog photography, video installation and experimental documentary video.

Columns.Title: Profile
Paragraphs: Visual artist with international recognition for the creation of artistic projects. Experience in teaching and content creation, with knowledge of sculpture, jewelry, photography, video, drawing and painting. Skilled in Final Cut Pro, Adobe Premiere and Photoshop, pedagogical analysis and the design of academic arts programs. Strengths include creativity, innovation and teamwork.

Title: Cxacxa
Paragraphs: “Cxacxa” pays tribute to Nasa Yuwe, the language of the Nasa people, also known as the Páez, who live in Colombia's Cauca department, especially the Tierradentro region. Cxacxa is a word with a deeply symbolic meaning: strength.

This experimental mosaic is made with metal studs bought in central Bogotá. A symbol of resistance, the stud has been embraced since the 1970s by urban subcultures seeking to reclaim industrial materials. I use it to create pixel-art figures inspired by the Nasa worldview. Red and green represent the blood of their ancestors and the natural world of their territory. Silver, by contrast, symbolizes technology, creating a dialogue between ancestral memory and the contemporary world.

Today, 65 Indigenous languages are spoken in Colombia and approximately 800 throughout the Americas. By creating “Cxacxa” in Nasa Yuwe, I seek to celebrate the strength of Nasa culture and the Indigenous presence within the worldview of contemporary art.
